inspector.title: SECURITY CONTROL INSPECTOR
inspector.rationale_default: This control provides defense-in-depth security measures at the designated architectural boundary.

debrief.rationale_validated: Architecture validated. Observed mitigation ({mitigation}%) satisfied the required architecture constraints.
debrief.rationale_violation: Architecture violated operational constraints. Latency budget passed: {latency}. Availability constraint passed: {availability}.

parameterized_queries.name: Parameterized Queries
parameterized_queries.why_failed: Parameterized Queries protect the SQL execution boundary against injection by separating code from data. They do not reduce the amount of data returned by a legitimate query.
parameterized_queries.demonstrates: SQL Injection and Excessive Data Exposure are different threat classes requiring controls at different architectural layers. Input protection does not guarantee output privacy.

input_sanitization.name: Input Sanitization
input_sanitization.why_failed: Removes dangerous characters from requests, but is ineffective against application logic flaws, data over-fetching, or semantic AI attacks that use natural language.
input_sanitization.demonstrates: Gateway-level filtering cannot fix backend architectural vulnerabilities.

rate_limiting_strict.name: Strict Rate Limiting
rate_limiting_strict.why_failed: Rate limiting restricts volumetric abuse such as brute force and DDoS. A single well-crafted request containing a logic flaw, SQL injection, or AI prompt bypass will succeed regardless of frequency limits.
rate_limiting_strict.demonstrates: Network-layer controls cannot inspect or sanitize application-layer payloads.

waf_rule_heavy.name: Heavy Signature WAF
waf_rule_heavy.why_failed: Blocks known attack signatures at the perimeter. It cannot protect against internal business logic flaws, legitimate-looking data over-exposure, or semantic AI attacks.
waf_rule_heavy.demonstrates: Perimeter defenses lack the application context needed to prevent logic-based vulnerabilities.

data_masking.name: Field-Level PII Masking
data_masking.why_failed: Data masking obfuscates sensitive fields in the response payload. It offers zero protection against unauthorized command execution or malicious input payloads reaching the database.
data_masking.demonstrates: Output redaction does not secure the execution environment against injection vectors.

differential_privacy.name: Differential Privacy Filter
differential_privacy.why_failed: Adds statistical noise to datasets to protect individual identities. It is irrelevant for preventing infrastructure exploits or SQL injections.
differential_privacy.demonstrates: Privacy controls are not interchangeable with structural security controls.

semantic_guardrails.name: Semantic Input Guardrails
semantic_guardrails.why_failed: Evaluates prompt intent for AI systems. Adds massive latency overhead and is useless for standard web vulnerabilities like SQL injection or excessive data exposure.
semantic_guardrails.demonstrates: AI middleware is highly domain-specific and introduces heavy operational trade-offs if misused.

output_content_filters.name: AI Output Content Filters
output_content_filters.why_failed: Validates the output of an AI agent to prevent unauthorized data generation. Does not prevent the initial injection or protect standard databases.
output_content_filters.demonstrates: Output validation must be paired with input validation to achieve true Defense-in-Depth.

static_analysis_bandit.name: Static Analysis (Bandit)
static_analysis_bandit.why_failed: The code contains insecure patterns detected by static analysis.
static_analysis_bandit.demonstrates: Static analysis identifies vulnerabilities in the source code before execution.

dependency_analysis_safety.name: Dependency Analysis (Safety)
dependency_analysis_safety.why_failed: The project uses dependencies with known security vulnerabilities.
dependency_analysis_safety.demonstrates: SCA identifies supply chain risks in third-party packages.

threat.title: Telemetry Filtering
threat.scenario: Imagine that you are processing security telemetry containing valid observations and noisy or discarded values.
threat.objective: Use iteration, conditions and accumulation to isolate valid observations and calculate a security metric.

step1.question: Which control structure iterates through each item in the list?
step1.hint: Use a for loop to scan every element in the sequence.

step2.question: What statement checks if the current number is positive?
